notes:
CRM notes (shorthand):
- inbound SMB, support product; looking to add a lightweight chat assistant into their web widget (react).
- primary contact: Elena Martin (Head of Product) - cautious about storing any PII in prompts.
- quoted: 'We need to make sure users can opt out of data collection and prompts are not retained longer than 30 days.'
- technical: currently using AWS us-east-1, want hosted API; no plans for private deployment now. Cost sensitive — esp. token costs on chat sessions.
- retention asks: TTL for request logs, opt-out/opt-in toggles at user level, deletion API (or retention-by-tag), and explicit statement that Redwood hosted API will not use customer prompts to train models (or want opt-out).
- legal flagged: need exportable audit logs + SSO/SAML + retention SLA for trial customers before procurement.
- SE notes: show how prefix caching can be disabled per-route; show server-side redaction patterns (PII remove) and tokenization cost estimate for 50 concurrent users.
- next: send tailored privacy FAQ + 30-day retention example + sample Data Processing Addendum (DPA) stub. Schedule 3/16 demo (15m) with Elena and infra lead.
use_case_summary: Goal: lightweight customer-facing chat to reduce repetitive tickets. Must meet privacy/opt-out needs. Low latency but prioritizes clear retention policy over aggressive caching.
prompt_storage_questions: Customer questions: Are raw prompts logged? If so, for how long? Can we opt-out per-tenant or per-user? Is there an API to purge prompts/requests? Are prompts used for model training?
log_retention_policy_requested: Customer prefers default 30 days, with option to reduce to 7 days for sensitive tenants and immediate purge on legal/DSR requests.
opt_out_requirements: Per-user opt-out toggle; admin console toggle for tenant; audit trail for opt-out changes; confirmation email template for users that opt out.
commercial_notes: SMB pilot expected to be low ARR initially, potential to expand to Dedicated if compliance demands increase. Close-criteria: DPA + clear retention SLA + demo acceptance.
sales_play: Offer hosted_api free credits, + privacy FAQ, + low-touch DPA template; position Redwood as production-first but privacy-aware. Recommend follow-up cadence: 1 week after privacy doc sent.
additional_context: They run a small legal + infra team (2 people). Main risk: legal will push back on any language that permits training on customer data. If we can provide an explicit opt-out and deletion API, likely to proceed to paid pilot.
